summary: An FYI document that points readers to the published standards of the MIT X Consortium for the X Window System. It is informational and a reference list rather than a specification.

plainLanguage.summary: This FYI document points readers to published standards and draft standards from the MIT X Consortium. It lists each document's title and version, and notes that draft standards could change as implementations were developed.

subtitle: A directory of published and draft standards from the MIT X Consortium.

tldr.problem: Readers needed pointers to the MIT X Consortium's published standards and draft standards.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists documents by title and version and distinguishes standards from draft standards that still required working implementations.
tldr.outcome: It serves as an informational guide to the listed X Consortium documents, not as a specification itself.

today: RFC 1198 is Informational and points to X Consortium standards and draft standards published at the time. It does not specify an Internet standard.

sections.title: Published X Consortium Standards
sections.content:
RFC 1198 provides pointers to published standards of the MIT X Consortium. The list includes the X Window System Protocol, Xlib, X Toolkit Intrinsics, Bitmap Distribution Format, Inter-Client Communication Conventions Manual, Compound Text Encoding, X Logical Font Description Conventions, X Display Manager Control Protocol, and the X11 Nonrectangular Window Shape Extension.

For each item, the memo gives its title and version or release where shown.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC lists published X Consortium documents and their versions. It is a directory to those documents, not a new X specification.

sections.title: Draft Standards and Availability
sections.content:
The RFC separately lists the PEX Protocol Specification and an extension for double-buffering, multi-buffering, and stereo as draft standards. It says these needed further proof of concept through working implementations and could change incompatibly if implementation work found significant problems.

The memo says standards and draft standards were generally included in the MIT X software distribution, which was available by anonymous FTP from various hosts or on tape from MIT.
sections.plainLanguage: The two draft documents still needed working implementations and could change. The RFC also explains how the X Consortium's documents and software distribution could be obtained.

sections.title: Status of the FYI
sections.content: RFC 1198 is an FYI document that provides information about MIT X Consortium publications. It does not specify an Internet standard.
sections.plainLanguage: This is an informational list of X Consortium publications. It does not define an Internet standard.
